candidates.name: Gediminas Castle
candidates.content: This is the Upper Castle of a complex of three built from the 13th century, much bashed about, and abandoned from the 16th. (The Lower Castle became the site of the Arsenal, Palace and Cathedral, and the "Crooked Castle" was destr

candidates.name: New Arsenal
candidates.content: The New Arsenal was established in the 18th century and mostly served as a barracks. It's now part of the National Museum displaying Lithuania's history and cultural heritage. As of October 2025, it is closed for major restructuri

candidates.name: Vilnius Cathedral
candidates.alt: Basilica of St Stanislaus and St Ladislaus of Vilnius
candidates.content: The first cathedral was built here in 1251, reverting to pagan worship in 1263. Fire destroyed a second in 1419, a third in 1530 and a fourth in 1610. Many parts of the fifth survive, notably the baroque chapel of St Casimir, but

candidates.name: Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania
candidates.content: This is a modern replica: the original was built in the 15th century, ruined in the 17th and demolished in 1801. A merchant's house was then built, which became part of the Arsenal. In the 1990s after independence the palace was r

candidates.name: Museum of Occupations and Freedom Fights
candidates.content: This is in the former KGB headquarters, where over 1000 were put to death. In spite of the plurals, it is specifically the Lithuanian experience under Soviet rule that is described; the experience under Nazism would reveal a very

candidates.name: Museum of Applied Arts & Design
candidates.content: This arsenal in the Lower Castle was built in the 15th century and stored heavy artillery. It's now part of the National Museum, displaying the country's pre-history and early history until the arrival of Christianity in the 11th

candidates.name: Presidential Palace
candidates.content: An 18th-century palace which is the seat of the President of Lithuania. Guided tours are available at weekends, and the palace is also open to the public on Open House days.

candidates.name: Gate of Dawn
candidates.content: The last survivor of the walled city's nine gates, various called Medininkai Gate as the street led south to that village, Sharp Gate, and now Gate of Dawn. It's straddled by a chapel with a large icon of the Virgin Mary, painted

candidates.name: St Anne's Church
candidates.content: Small flamboyant church in Gothic style, built by 1500 and little altered since. There is a legend that when Napoleon's campaigns brought him to Vilnius, he declared that he'd like to lift the church on his palm and carry it back

candidates.name: Cathedral of the Theotokos
candidates.alt: Dievo Motinos Ėmimo į Dangų katedra
candidates.content: Like St Anne's, this stands by an entrance bridge to Užupis. It was first built in the 1340s by Grand Duke Algirdas before the country became Christian. It's been destroyed, rebuilt and changed use several times - in the 1820s it

candidates.name: Church of Saints Peter and Paul
candidates.content: The first church from around 1500 was wooden and burned down, and its successor was wrecked in the 1650s in the war with Russia. The present building was commissioned by Michał Kazimierz Pac (1624-82), begun in 1668 but only compl

candidates.name: Church of St Philip and St Jacob
candidates.alt: Šv Apaštalų Pilypo ir Jokūbo bažnyčia
candidates.content: Red and white Baroque church of the Dominican order, completed in 1722. It houses a large icon of the Virgin Mary "Hodegetria" - in iconography this means "shows the way" as she points to the infant as the salvation of mankind.

candidates.name: Seimas Palace
candidates.content: This complex houses the Lithuanian parliament. The first building, completed in 1980, was the seat of the Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic, and looks it. In 2007 the new Parliament Hall (or Building 2) was opened. Building 3 w

candidates.name: Church of St Catherine
candidates.content: Built in the 18th century in Baroque style and dedicated to Saint Catherine of Alexandria, as part of a Benedictine Nunnery. The church is known for its elegant façade, intricate stucco decorations, but many of its artworks were e

candidates.name: Church of Our Lady of the Sign
candidates.content: Built in Neo-Byzantine style in 1903, this is the Eastern Orthodox church you see when looking west along Gedimino prospekt. It was financed by fundraising around the Russian Empire.

candidates.name: Contemporary Art Centre
candidates.content: This has a permanent display of Fluxus artwork plus other rotating exhibitions.

candidates.name: Old Arsenal
candidates.content: This arsenal in the Lower Castle was built in the 15th century and stored heavy artillery. It's now part of the National Museum, displaying the country's pre-history and early history until the arrival of Christianity in the 11th

candidates.name: Vilnius University
candidates.content: Vilnius University now has faculties across the city and beyond, but this is the baroque core of it, with the library, courtyards, observatory and Church of St Johns (plural: Šv Jono, the Baptist and the Evangelist). You can see t

candidates.name: House of the Signatories
candidates.content: Neo-renaissance mansion where Lithuania's Act of Independence was signed on 16 February 1918. It's now a branch of the National Museum depicting the story of Lithuania as a separate nation, in which independent spirit it makes few

candidates.name: Kazys Varnelis House-Museum
candidates.content: Varnelis (1917-2020) was an abstract artist who mostly lived in the USA, returning to Vilnius in 1998. His house is now part of National Museum, displaying his studio and works.

candidates.name: Bastion of Vilnius Defensive Wall
candidates.content: The city walls were built 1503-22 with nine gates (of which only Gate of Dawn survives) and this artillery position. It's now a museum of the city's military history.

candidates.name: Pushkin Museum
candidates.content: Alexander Pushkin (1799-1837) was often in exile around the edges of Russia: not here, but his son lived in this mansion. His works were translated into Lithuanian and much of the museum is about that literary task, but it has per

candidates.name: Railway Museum
candidates.content: Presents the history of railways in Lithuania from Prussian times until today. Railway equipment small enough to fit into a room, tickets, staff uniforms and the like are on display in addition to scale models, pictures and videos

candidates.name: Energy and Technology Museum
candidates.content: This was the city's first power plant, opened in 1903. It exhibits electricity generation, industrial technologies, child-friendly interactions and transformation, the Tesla-inspired wizardry that enables long-distance transmissio

candidates.name: Toy Museum
candidates.content: Interactive museum of toys down the ages, chid-friendly of course.

candidates.name: National Museum of Art
candidates.content: Huge display of art from the 14th to 20th century.

candidates.name: Museums Centre for Information, Digitisation and LIMIS
candidates.content: About the digitisation and online curating of museum collections. So if you want to grasp the "principles of the use of ontologies" you've come to the right place, but if you seek physical exhibits you've not been listening.

candidates.name: Culinary Museum
candidates.content: This is about tableware rather than cuisine.

candidates.name: Lithuanian Opera and Ballet Theatre
candidates.content: Grand ornate opera house with three or four weekly performances.

candidates.name: Lindyhop Klubas
candidates.content: Lindy Hop is a US swing / jazz dance style that evolved from the 1930s and is now enjoying a revival, with clubs and lessons, retro gear optional.

candidates.name: Oskaras Koršunovas Theatre (OKT)
candidates.content: Avant garde theatre southwest edge of Old Town,.

candidates.name: Old Theatre of Vilnius
candidates.content: Creaky but atmospheric old theatre with performances mostly in Russian.

candidates.name: BIX
candidates.content: Bar founded by BIX rock band. Live rock / metal bands on Friday nights, karaoke on Thursdays, and rock music any time on the dance floor. Surprisingly good food.

candidates.name: Alaus Namai
candidates.content: Big saloon offering beer from less-known Lithuanian brands.

candidates.name: Artistai
candidates.content: The large courtyard is a great place to relax and watch the sunset. Friendly service, live music.

candidates.name: Šnekutis
candidates.content: Long-table like a beer hall, with trad beer and food.

candidates.name: Soho Club
candidates.content: LGBT club, gets very crowded.

candidates.name: Kiras
candidates.content: Café in 1970s style, with happy memories of Soviet days: "chaika" a tea-house is a pun on "cheka" the secret police. They have another café at Pylimo 21b.

candidates.name: Buga Sotu
candidates.content: Trad food: chicken, dumplings, kibinai, pizzas and carp. Live music on Friday and sometimes on Saturday. You'd most likely eat here if you visited the TV Tower and baulked at their restaurant prices.

candidates.name: Vegafè
candidates.content: Vegan cafe.

candidates.name: Pilies kepyklėlė
candidates.content: Café-bakery in the university building near Saints John.

candidates.name: Kamikadzė Japonų virtuvė
candidates.content: Japanese restaurant with the usual offerings.

candidates.name: Plus Plus Plus Gastrobaras
candidates.content: This is the most central of a fast-food chain.

candidates.name: Dėvėti
candidates.content: Calls itself a gastropub, more like a bar with pizza and pita bread sandwiches.

candidates.name: RadhaRane
candidates.content: Vegetarian Indian restaurant with a good menu choice.

candidates.name: Wok to Walk
candidates.content: This is the main outlet of an Asian cuisine franchise.

candidates.name: Fėjų kepyklėlė
candidates.content: Bakery-cafe with pastries, snacks, pizza and ice cream. It's infested with Lithuanian fairies, which you'll either adore or upchuck over.

candidates.name: Medininkai
candidates.content: Lithuanian food near Gate of Dawn, it got good reviews to 2022 but now feels tourist-trappy.

candidates.name: Balzac
candidates.content: Traditional French cuisine, well prepared, great atmosphere.

candidates.name: Lokys
candidates.content: Specializes in Lithuanian traditional cuisine and game.

candidates.name: Halės turgus
candidates.content: The main market hall of Vilnius, built in 1906 and looking like a railway terminus. Inside, its east side has food stalls and a couple of eateries. Adjacent is the modern wing for clothing and household wares.

december.text: St Nicholas Church: A Russian Orthodox church. Not to be confused with the RC St Nicholas on Šv Mikalojaus.
St Nicholas Church: The Roman Catholic St Nick's, brick gothic, and the oldest church in Vilnius being documented in 1387.
Akropolis: Large mall with multiplex cinema and ice rink.
